arxiv-1805-03441.title: Machine Learning in Compiler Optimisation
arxiv-1805-03441.creator: Zheng Wang, Michael O’Boyle
arxiv-1805-03441.description: Abstract In the last decade, machine learning based compilation has moved from an an obscure research niche to a mainstream activity. In this article, we describe the relationship between machine learning and compiler optimisation and introduce the main concepts of features, models, training and deployment.

arxiv-2210-03985.title: Bird-Eye Transformers for Text Generation Models
arxiv-2210-03985.creator: Lei Sha, Yuhang Song, Yordan Yordanov, Tommaso Salvatori, Thomas Lukasiewicz
arxiv-2210-03985.description: Abstract Transformers have become an indispensable module for text generation models since their great success in machine translation. Previous works attribute the success of transformers to the query-key-value dot-product attention, which provides a robust inductive bias by the fully connected token graphs. However, we found that self-attention has a severe limitation.

arxiv-2306-08980.title: The upper bound of information diffusion in code review Journal: Empirical Software Engineering
arxiv-2306-08980.creator: Michael Dorner, Daniel Mendez, Krzysztof Wnuk, Ehsan Zabardast, Jacek Czerwonka
arxiv-2306-08980.description: Abstract Background: Code review, the discussion around a code change among humans, forms a communication network that enables its participants to exchange and spread information. Although reported by qualitative studies, our understanding of the capability of code review as a communication network is still limited.

arxiv-2405-17939.title: Detecting and removing bloated dependencies in CommonJS packages
arxiv-2405-17939.creator: Yuxin Liu, Deepika Tiwari, Cristian Bogdan, Benoit Baudry
arxiv-2405-17939.description: Abstract JavaScript packages are notoriously prone to bloat, a factor that significantly impacts the performance and maintainability of web applications. While web bundlers and tree-shaking can mitigate this issue in client-side applications, state-of-the-art techniques have limitations on the detection and removal of bloat in server-side applications.

arxiv-2406-07959.title: Multicriteria Adjustable Robustness
arxiv-2406-07959.creator: Elisabeth Halser, Elisabeth Finhold, Neele Leithäuser, Jan Schwientek, Katrin Teichert, Karl-Heinz Küfer
arxiv-2406-07959.description: Abstract Multicriteria adjustable robust optimization (MARO) problems arise in a wide variety of practical settings, for example, in the design of a building’s energy supply. However, no general approaches, neither for the characterization of solutions to this problem class, nor potential solution methods, are available in the literature so far.

arxiv-2410-00061.title: Neural Decompiling of Tracr Transformers
arxiv-2410-00061.creator: Hannes Thurnherr, Kaspar Riesen
arxiv-2410-00061.description: Abstract Recently, the transformer architecture has enabled substantial progress in many areas of pattern recognition and machine learning. However, as with other neural network models, there is currently no general method available to explain their inner workings. The present paper represents a first step towards this direction.

arxiv-2410-03569.title: Making Hard Problems Easier with Custom Data Distributions and Loss Regularization: A Case Study in Modular Arithmetic
arxiv-2410-03569.creator: Eshika Saxena, Alberto Alfarano, François Charton, Zeyuan Allen-Zhu, Emily Wenger, Kristin Lauter
arxiv-2410-03569.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Eshika Saxena, Alberto Alfarano, François Charton, Zeyuan Allen-Zhu, Emily Wenger, Kristin Lauter. Recent work showed that ML-based attacks on Learning with Errors (LWE), a hard problem used in post-quantum cryptography, outperform classical algebraic attacks in certain settings. Although promising, ML attacks struggle to scale to more complex LWE settings. Prior work connected this issue to the difficulty of training ML models to do modular arithmetic, a core feature of the LWE problem.

pmc-11744372.title: Interim Analysis of a Prospective Polysomnographic Study of Weighted Blankets in Patients with Psychophysiological Insomnia
pmc-11744372.creator: Gülçin Benbir Şenel, Derya Karadeniz
pmc-11744372.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundWeighted blankets have recently introduced in the treatment on insomnia as a non-pharmacological integrative therapy. Here we prospectively evaluated the effects of weighted blankets on the sleep structure and heart rate variability (HRV) in patients with primary psychophysiological insomnia.MethodsIn this prospective polysomnographic (PSG) study between August 2021 and August 2022, patients were given weighted blankets (~10% of body weight) to use at home for 10 nights consecutively.

pmc-12557801.title: Exploring family health, support, self-efficacy and quality of life during the cancer trajectory: a protocol for a longitudinal mixed methods multi-centre cohort study
pmc-12557801.creator: Lærke K Tolstrup, Nana Hyldig, Soren Moller, Mette Stie, Mette Kjerholt, Mary Jarden, Karin Piil, Elisabeth Coyne, Cristina Garcia-Vivar, Barbara Voltelen, Trine Munk-Olsen, Karin Brochstedt Dieperink
pmc-12557801.description: IntroductionA cancer diagnosis not only profoundly impacts individuals but also the very core of their families, reshaping their lives in many ways. However, there is a lack of focus on the well-being and health of the entire family across adult cancer research.

pmc-12579351.title: Comparison of Investigations Following Inpatient and Outpatient Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography and Their Impact on Complication Rates and Length of Hospital Stay: A Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-12579351.creator: Owen Morris, Luc Nyunt
pmc-12579351.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionEndoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) is a therapeutic procedure for conditions affecting the biliary and pancreatic ductal systems. Complications include post-ERCP pancreatitis (PEP), cholangitis, and bleeding, which typically present within the first few hours post-procedure.

pmc-13233807.title: Drivers of disparities in asthma exacerbation and healthcare utilization: a quantitative analysis of neighborhood deprivation in Southern California, United States
pmc-13233807.creator: Stanley Xu, Fagen Xie, Daniel A. Powers, Eric J. Puttock, Michael Schatz, William M. Vollmer, Robert S. Zeiger, Wansu Chen
pmc-13233807.description: ObjectiveWhile prior studies showed lower socioeconomic status was associated with worse acute asthma exacerbations (AAE) and asthma-related emergency department/urgent care (ED/UC) visits, few have quantified contributions of risk factors. We aim to identify and quantify risk factors driving these disparities across levels of neighborhood deprivation.

pmc-13271539.title: Critical appraisal of intravitreal triamcinolone acetonide for serpiginous-like choroiditis in a tuberculosis-endemic setting
pmc-13271539.creator: Srinivasan Sanjay
pmc-13271539.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). on bias, which is only briefly acknowledged in the limitations. Of 32 initially identified patients, only 14 (15 eyes) with at least 6 months of follow-up were included in the analysis, yet there is no systematic comparison between included and excluded patients, raising concern about attrition bias and potential overestimation of benefit if early failures or complications were more likely to be lost.

pmc-13286748.title: Aggression mediates the association between problematic smartphone use and cyberbullying perpetration: a 6-year longitudinal study of Korean adolescents
pmc-13286748.creator: Hyunjoo Na, Hye Seung Choi, Il Hyun Lee, Gyungjoo Lee
pmc-13286748.description: IntroductionCyberbullying perpetration is a form of interpersonal violence among adolescents that is associated with mental health risk factors and outcomes, yet the longitudinal mechanisms linking problematic smartphone use (PSU) to cyberbullying remain unclear. Guided by the General Aggression Model, this study examined whether aggression mediates the relationship between PSU and cyberbullying perpetration and whether parental structuring moderates this indirect pathway.

pmc-13296305.title: Possible Triggering of Molecular Mimicry by Environmental Pollution
pmc-13296305.creator: Sofya Mishina, Bryttan Adams, Bruce Uhal, Yun Liang

pmc-13342318.title: Moving beyond discrete categories in motor cognition
pmc-13342318.creator: Roland Pfister, Greg Huffman, James R. Brockmole
pmc-13342318.description: Theories on human action control assume the human mind copes with the computational challenge of selecting and performing goal-directed movements by recycling previous action plans. Feature binding assists this recycling by integrating stimulus and response features into episodic representations. Perhaps surprisingly, however, previous evidence for binding and retrieval is confined to categorical perceptual and motor features that define coarse-grained decisions.

pmc-13473531.title: A TriNetX global collaborative network retrospective cohort study on the impact of COVID-19 vaccination on juvenile idiopathic arthritis
pmc-13473531.creator: Su-Boon Yong, Ping-Hao Chiang, Chi Ya Yang, Ji Hung Wei, Chia-Jung Li, Chih-Wei Tseng, Shiow-Ing Wang, James Cheng-Chung Wei, Jiu-Yao Wang
pmc-13473531.description: The objective is to determine the Impact of COVID-19 Vaccination and Medical Utilization in Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (JIA) patients. Our study retrieved data from the US Collaborative Network in TriNetX between January 1st, 2020, and June 30th, 2023. We investigated the incidence of COVID-19, medical utilization, and mortality in JIA patients.

pmc-13537271.title: A MAP-SNARE interaction links cortical microtubules to the exocytic fusion machinery during auxin-dependent growth remodeling
pmc-13537271.creator: Jia Deng, Jing Qin, Panpan Wang, Xiaojing Zhao, Xinyuan Zhang, Jingyan Fu, Tonglin Mao, Xiangfeng Wang
pmc-13537271.description: Auxin exerts diverse physiological effects through local maxima and tissue-scale gradients established by directional transport, which depends on the plasma membrane (PM) distribution and vesicular trafficking of auxin transporters. Cortical microtubules are positioned beneath the PM and have been implicated in trafficking events. However, how microtubules interface with terminal vesicle trafficking machinery at the PM remains unclear.

pmc-13538357.title: The impact of PM2.5 component exposure during early pregnancy on congenital heart disease: evidence from Guangdong, China
pmc-13538357.creator: Yanbing Chen, Peiming Su, Qixian Gu, Huili Wei, Jialing Qiu, Guangming Tan
pmc-13538357.description: Limited is known about how the components of particulate matter with aerodynamic diameter < 2.5 μm (PM2.5) are related to congenital heart disease (CHD). We aimed to demonstrate the relationship between exposure to PM2.5 components during early pregnancy and the risk of CHD. This study included 2,601,300 live births and stillbirths in Guangdong, China from 2014 to 2017.
